note: Vol. I No. 40. Pages 1-2 are the standing card columns and national reprint; the town is on pages 1 (column 1, the merchants' cards) and 3. Page 3 columns 3 and 5 are the Tesseract fallback and are NOT interleaved, which is why the ordinances, the militia election and the prices current are quoted from there; columns 1, 2, 4 and 6 are the Vision reading, where the segmenter alternates two physical columns line by line and an advertisement survives as a cut half. `locator.lines` is the whole advertisement; `lines_of_claim` is the subset quoted.

The same advertisement at 1834-09-10 page 3 column 4 carries the word 'Franklin' at line 2812, three lines from '[uncertain: ICE second door west from]' and '[uncertain: ruth Water-streets.]' — and THERE it is not the address: that column interleaves the prices current, whose entries 'Stone,' and 'Wood' sit at lines 2815-2816 immediately below it, and 'Franklin' in that list is the Franklin stove. T-0290's August read then found the address printed whole in its own sentence — 'of Franklin and South Water.st', 1834-08-20 page 3 column 4 lines 3272-3276 — which is a witness the stove cannot explain, so the corner is closed on that evidence and cited to it. Both facts stand: the 09-10 'Franklin' really is a stove, and the office really is at Franklin and South Water. The initial G. is from the same man's own 'For Sale' notice in this issue (c005), and the 1833 copy date is the August witness's, which reads 'Churo, Do. 17. 1333'.

claims.notes: ONE IMPRESSION OF THE STANDING LAKE STREET LAND-AGENCY CARD. The Democrat sets this advertisement, word for word the same, in every issue from 1834-05-14 to 1834-10-01 — twenty consecutive weeks, eighteen of which set the line ‘purchased and Sold, or by commi[s]sion’ recognisably (T-1051). The card is identified by its copy and not by its display line: the same trade (‘House and Land Agent’), the same offer of building lots in the town and the School Section, the same houses to let, and the same office on Lake street opposite Dr. Temple's. The display line is transcribed '[uncertain: 1% 0. ?A?A]' (3184) — the transcription's own question marks, kept — and nothing is read off it. THE PROPRIETOR'S NAME IS NOT READ HERE and none is supplied into the quote: the record's ‘W. G. Blanchard’ stands on T-0408's reading of the two impressions whose columns are NOT Tesseract fallbacks (1834-07-16 line 5527, 1834-09-17 line 3292) and on identity.json's declared firm merge, not on this impression. The card is set out of order, 'A sion.' (3186) standing above the line it completes (3187); the normalization puts it back and the quote does not. Neither the houses to let nor the address is in this column, so this printing is recorded as silent about placement.
